conversations.answer: The error "module is not defined" indicates that you are trying to use Node.js-style module exports in a client-side context. The module.exports syntax is common in Node.js for exporting functions or objects for use in other files, but it isn't available natively in the browser environment.You can use a different method to export your functions if you want them to be accessible elsewhere, or you can simply remove the module.exports line if it isn't needed. For example, if you want these functions to be globally accessible, you could attach them to the window object:[CODE_BLOCK_0]Or you could remove the module.exports line entirely:[CODE_BLOCK_1]The decision should depend on how you plan to use these functions.If you do need to use Node.js-style modules on the client side, you will need to use a tool like Browserify or Webpack. These tools let you write modular code for the browser that can be bundled up into a single JavaScript file to include in your HTML.

conversations.answer: My apologies for the confusion earlier. You're right. There's nothing wrong with using Babel or Webpack. Jest will run your tests, making use of the compiled code.

conversations.answer: This error is occurring because the document object is also a part of the web API and not available in a Node.js environment. conversations.prompt: why am i back to inlining javascript
conversations.answer: I apologize for the confusion. To avoid inlining JavaScript code in the HTML file and keep the separation of concerns intact, you can create a new initialization function in the game.js file that sets up the event listeners. Then, you can call this function in the HTML file.Here is how to do this:Modify game.js to export a function that sets up the event listeners:[CODE_BLOCK_0]Call initGame function in index.html:[CODE_BLOCK_1]This way, the JavaScript code related to the Game class remains in the game.js file, and the HTML file is only responsible for calling the initialization function, preserving the separation of concerns between HTML and JavaScript.
